title: State preparation via measurement and feedback: pushing relations, state structures, and non-invertible symmetries
authors: Yabo Li, Aditi Mitra, Tsung-Cheng Lu
abstract: Quantum circuits with measurements and unitary feedback (MF) can prepare long-range entangled states in constant depth, but a systematic construction of the MF preparation circuit for a given target state remains underexplored. We develop such a scheme for one-dimensional states, based on the notion of pushable defects: virtual-bond operators of a matrix product state that can be pushed through the tensor at the price of a physical feedback unitary. We show that the set of pushable defects, together with their pushing relations classifies finite-depth MF-preparable states and dictates their preparation circuits. To each class of the target state $|A\rangle$, we associate a state $|B\rangle$ from which $|A\rangle$ can be prepared using a 1-round MF circuit; in particular, $|A\rangle$ is preparable from a product state using a circuit with 1 round of MF whenever $|B\rangle$ is preparable by a finite-depth local unitary (FDLU) circuit. For a general target state, the scheme is obtained by iterating this procedure until the associated state is FDLU-preparable. For open-boundary matrix product states, the scheme is complete: it constructs a preparation circuit whenever finite-depth MF preparation with left-conditioned feedback corrections is possible. Pushable defects and pushing relations thus emerge as a unifying principle for quantum state preparation via measurements and feedback. This characterization further reveals an intrinsic connection between MF circuits and non-invertible symmetries: states with certain classes of pushing relations are related to a product state by Tambara-Yamagami duality operators, or by continuous cosine symmetry operators with fusion rules $L_α L_{α'} = L_{α+α'} + L_{α-α'}$, together with their generalizations up to (not necessarily transversal) gates.
summary: The paper introduces 'pushable defects' as a novel diagnostic tool to systematically classify quantum states preparable via Measurement and Feedback circuits on MPS. It shows that these defect relations dictate the necessary preparation circuit depth and reveals an intrinsic link between this process and non-invertible symmetries in condensed matter physics.
main_problem: The primary goal is developing a systematic theoretical framework to characterize quantum states preparable using Measurement and Feedback (MF) circuits, extending beyond existing protocols.
main_result: The authors establish that 'pushable defects' and their associated 'pushing relations' provide a unifying principle for classifying finite-depth MF-preparable states. This classification reveals deep connections between state preparation and non-invertible symmetries.
method: The methodology involves analyzing one-dimensional quantum systems using Matrix Product States (MPS) formalism, defining 'pushable defects' as virtual-bond operators that can be pushed through the tensor structure at the cost of a physical feedback unitary.
model_or_system: The model focuses on 1D quantum systems described by MPS. The preparation process alternates between local unitary operations (FDLU) and measurement/feedback rounds, analyzed via defect propagation in virtual bond spaces.
key_observables: Pushable defects, pushing relations, the rank of the transfer matrix ($T_{\mathcal{A}}$), and the associated symmetry operators (e.g., Tambara-Yamagami duality).
important_parameters: The number of measurement/feedback rounds required for preparation; coupling constants ($\lambda_i$) parameterizing the state structure.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that unwanted measurement outcomes can be compensated by feedback operations without requiring post-selection, and it builds upon characterizing defects in virtual spaces.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the sequential preparation of a target state using alternating FDLU and MF circuits; other figures likely detail defect propagation or symmetry relations.
paper_structure: The paper systematically develops the concept of pushable defects, first establishing conditions for single-round preparation (relating to FDLU states), then generalizing this iteratively for arbitrary depth, and finally connecting these structural constraints to underlying non-invertible symmetries.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful algebraic tool (defect analysis) to characterize the computational power of measurement-based quantum computation protocols in 1D systems, linking it directly to fundamental concepts like symmetry protection.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Sequential preparation of the target state |A⟩from |00 · · ·⟩using circuits with local measurements and feedback corrections. In the sequence, |B(j)⟩is prepared from |A(j)⟩using FDLU, and |A(j+1)⟩is prepared from |B(j)⟩using a single round of local measurements and feedback corrections.

FIG. 2. The preparation scheme we propose for the target state |A⟩, in which we perform a sequence of MF circuits on a certain initial FDLU-preparable state, generating a sequence of states {· · · , |C⟩, |B⟩, |A⟩}. The construction of the state sequence from the target state |A⟩is in reverse order: the pushable defects of |A⟩are used to construct |B⟩; the pushable defects of |B⟩are used to construct |C⟩, etc. As discussed in the main text, certain rounds of MF circuits can be replaced by an FDLU circuit, which suggests that this scheme includes the general circuit architecture shown in Fig. 1.

FIG. 3. When the virtual space is decomposed into four subspaces, respectively exhibiting pushing relations in class RIRI (green), RIRX (orange), RZRX (blue), and RILI (black), the MPS |A⟩is prepared from a product of multi-qudit states |ψΛ⟩ using a composition of parallel KW and KT dualities shown in this figure, up to transversal unitary circuit. The state structure for the RILI subspace is derived in Appendix E.
